findings.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset (items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) of the 6-char prefix that DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes as sessionType[0-1]+tokenType[2-3]+grantType[4-5]) and inverts the comparison by returning false when the slice equals the expected shortcut, so the new grant assertion is vacuous. For any correctly encoded ID the extracted slice is tokenType's 2nd char plus grantType's 1st char (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'), which never equals any expected shortcut ('ac','dg','rt','ci'), so the equals branch never fires and the matcher degenerates to 'colon-separated with UUID suffix' — expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken pass regardless of which grant shortcut (and entirely without checking) the sessionType/tokenType chars the token carries, and a regression issuing tokens with the wrong grant context fails no test; conversely, fixing only the offset while keeping the inverted equals would fail every token event in the suite.

[BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second check, whose message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', passes grantType instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId is never null-validated. A null rawTokenId passes the constructor's stated invariant and encodeTokenId silently produces a token ID ending in the literal ':null' (which decodes back as rawId 'null') instead of failing fast, and if the guard ever fires the misleading 'Null grantType not allowed' message sends debugging to the wrong parameter.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType actually exercises a NullPointerException, not the intended IllegalArgumentException: it never calls factory.postInit(), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory stays null and getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac") throws at sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) before reaching the explicit unknown-shortcut IllegalArgumentException branch. The broad catch (RuntimeException) swallows the NPE and the test is green while verifying none of the unknown-grant error contract; deleting the IllegalArgumentException branch entirely would still leave this test passing (the NPE, or the requireNonNull NPE from AccessTokenContext, satisfies the catch), so a regression in the unknown-grant error path ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId has no caller anywhere in this diff's production code — TokenManager.initToken only uses getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext and encodeTokenId — so the decode half of the encoder ships unused while the encode half is wired into every token issuance. Every newly issued access token gets a 6-char context prefix permanently baked into its jti (an externally visible format change that old nodes and stored tokens must tolerate) before any production consumer proves the round-trip end-to-end; defects in the decode contract (shortcut collisions, the strict length-6 check, legacy-ID handling) are validated only by unit tests, and discovering later that the format needs adjusting becomes a migration problem for already-issued tokens.

[ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts only from loaded OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances, and feature-gated grants (PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory gated on OID4VC_VCI, plus the EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory-implementing CibaGrantTypeFactory and DeviceGrantTypeFactory) are not loaded when their feature/config is off — while the lazy-refresh fallback in getGrantTypeByShortcut re-scans the same already-filtered getProviderFactoriesStream and can therefore never recover them. On a node where one of these grants is disabled, decoding a token ID carrying the 'pc'/'ci'/'dg' shortcut (issued by a node where the feature is enabled, e.g. a mixed-feature cluster once any decode consumer exists) throws IllegalArgumentException 'Unknown value ... for grant type', defeating the refresh mechanism whose stated purpose is handling grants not present in the startup maps.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the new sessionType/tokenType/grantType derivation logic — has no test in this diff that asserts its output: the unit test constructs the provider with a null session and covers only decode/encode round-trips, and the integration assertions on the encoded prefix are vacuous (see the AssertEvents matcher defect). A regression in the derivation (e.g. always classifying sessions as ONLINE/REGULAR, dropping the TRANSIENT check, or misreading the offline flag) passes the entire suite, and the mislabelled 6-char prefix would then be baked into every subsequently issued access token's jti before anyone notices.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) (grant occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix) and inverts the comparison (returns false when the extracted value EQUALS the expected shortcut), so the grant assertion is vacuous. The grant-type verification this diff adds to expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken verifies nothing: for any well-formed encoded ID, substring(3,5) is always '<tokenType-2nd-char><grant-1st-char>' (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'), which never equals 'ac'/'dg'/'rt'/'ci', so the matcher passes regardless of which grant was encoded — a regression encoding the wrong grant shortcut into every access token ID passes the whole testsuite. Additionally, if only the offset is later corrected, the inverted condition will reject every correctly encoded token, and a prefix shorter than 5 chars throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

[ADVISORY] The only test added for the encoder never exercises getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the provider is constructed with a null session (line 49) and every test method calls only getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId — so the derivation logic (offline vs online vs transient session type, lightweight vs regular token type, grant-type attribute fallback) has zero coverage; the test also hand-builds the grant maps instead of calling postInit, leaving the duplicate-shortcut startup validation untested. A regression in the derivation (e.g. an inverted isOffline() or persistence-state check, or a broken lightweight-token flag read) misencodes every newly issued token and nothing in this diff catches it: the unit test only round-trips hand-built contexts, and the AssertEvents matcher added in this diff checks ID shape but not prefix content, so the feature's actual output is unverified end-to-end.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second call (message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') re-checks grantType, so rawTokenId is never null-validated. A null rawTokenId passes validation and encodeTokenId silently produces IDs like 'onrtac:null' (string concatenation of null) instead of failing fast, corrupting the token ID namespace for any caller that passes a null raw ID; the mislabeled exception message also misleads whoever debugs the eventual failure.

[BUG] Only the token-minting paths touched in this diff set Constants.GRANT_TYPE; the legacy DefaultTokenExchangeProvider (served when the standard token exchange feature is disabled) and the UMA PermissionGrantType reach TokenManager's responseBuilder/initToken without setting it, so their access tokens fall into the 'na' fallback even though 'te'/'pg' shortcuts are registered for those grants. With legacy token exchange enabled, every exchanged token's encoded context misreports the grant as unknown, so consumers of the new decode API — the stated purpose of this framework — cannot identify token-exchange tokens, and the 'te'/'pg' shortcuts are dead mappings on those paths; the PR fixed this exact gap for StandardTokenExchangeProvider and PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType but missed the sibling paths.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when a grant shortcut cannot be resolved, because the lazy refresh in getGrantTypeByShortcut only scans currently-registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances — so token IDs minted while a feature-gated grant was enabled ('pc' gated on OID4VC_VCI per PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory.isSupported, plus 'dg'/'ci' which are EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory) become unresolvable once that feature is disabled or the provider is removed. The backward-compatibility design handles old colon-less IDs (UNKNOWN fallback) but not provider lifecycle: once any consumer of this decode API ships, historical tokens issued before a feature toggle flip throw instead of degrading to UNKNOWN like old-format IDs do, and during rolling deploys with mixed feature state different nodes disagree on the same token ID.

[ADVISORY] The lazy registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType (lines 113-114) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 131-132) put entries into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit performs, so a newly registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the existing grant's mapping. In exactly the scenario this code targets ('Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed'), a colliding shortcut replaces the previous grant's entry with no error, and decoding tokens of the previously-registered grant then returns the wrong grant type — the startup IllegalStateException guard is bypassed precisely when a collision actually occurs.

[BUG] AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and inverts the comparison (returns false on equality), so the grant-shortcut assertion never validates anything. All four updated expectations (code, device, refresh, CIBA) pass vacuously for any colon-separated UUID: a regression that mints 'na' or a wrong grant shortcut into TOKEN_ID sails through the suite, and fixing only the offset would make every correctly encoded token (e.g. 'onrtac:...' where substring(4,6)=='ac') fail the matcher via the inverted branch.

[BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second check, whose message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', re-validates grantType so rawTokenId is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId silently mints token IDs ending in the literal ':null'; no current caller trips it, but the guard this constructor exists to enforce is unenforced for exactly one of its four fields.

[ADVISORY] The PR deletes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) — work not traceable to the context-encoding requirement. Extensions compiled against server-spi-private that copy a Context break at compile time on upgrade; the traceable alternative (adding this.grantType = context.grantType to the existing constructor) would have preserved the API and avoided copies silently dropping the new field.

[ADVISORY] Grant-type coverage relies on five hand-maintained setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...) call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, TokenManager.validateToken, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider) with a silent 'na' fallback in the encoder. Nothing enforces that every token-minting path records its grant — any future grant or path that forgets the attribute encodes 'na' into token IDs with no error, log, or failing test, so the encoded context silently degrades to unknown.

[ADVISORY] The decode half of the framework ships with no production caller — getTokenContextFromTokenId is invoked only from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest. The stated payoff (retrieving session/token/grant context from the token instead of proprietary claims) is inert in this diff, and the public SPI shape is locked in before any real consumer has exercised it, so a later consumer will discover design mismatches after the API is frozen.

[ADVISORY] The access token jti format changes globally from a UUID to '<st><tt><gt>:<uuid>' with no feature flag, realm option, or provider configuration to disable the new format. During rolling upgrades a cluster emits two ID formats, and external consumers of jti or the TOKEN_ID event detail that assume UUIDs (an assumption Keycloak's own test suite encoded until this diff) have no opt-out short of a version downgrade.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are unreachable after postInit (which enumerates the same getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) source) and bypass the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit performs. Dead code on all reachable states; if it were ever reached via a late-registered grant, it silently overwrites existing shortcut mappings (a colliding shortcut rebinds e.g. 'ac' away from authorization_code) without the startup validation firing.

[ADVISORY] The unit test bypasses postInit and hand-stubs the grant maps with 3 of 10 grants, so testIncorrectGrantType treats 'ac' — a valid production grant shortcut — as unknown. The test asserts against a registry that diverges from the real one, so a regression in the factory's actual grant registration or in the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation passes the suite while breaking production encoding.

[BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — line 73 carries the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' but tests grantType, so the rawTokenId null-guard is dead code. A null rawTokenId passes validation and encodeTokenId silently produces a token ID ending in ':null' (getTokenContextFromTokenId on it returns the literal string 'null' as rawTokenId) instead of failing fast like the other three constructor guards; the invariant the check exists to enforce is unenforced.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) — one character left of the grant shortcut, which encodeTokenId places at indices 4-5 — and inverts the comparison, returning false when the extracted characters EQUAL the expected shortcut instead of when they differ. The matcher passes for a token ID carrying ANY grant shortcut (e.g. expectCodeToToken accepts a password-grant token), so the four updated helpers (code, device, refresh, CIBA) assert nothing about the grant encoded into Details.TOKEN_ID and the suite stays green if TokenManager encodes the wrong or no grant; it only fails on coincidental character overlap (chars 3-4 equal to the expected shortcut, e.g. expecting 'rt' against an '...rtte' prefix).

[ADVISORY] The encoding is wired into initToken unconditionally (no feature flag) and this diff contains no production caller of getTokenContextFromTokenId — the framework changes every access token's jti format while nothing can read the context back. All tokens system-wide (including realms that never use lightweight tokens) permanently carry the 6-char prefix, while the decode half — strict length/shortcut validation and the grant registry — ships exercised only by unit tests with hand-built maps; any flaw there surfaces only when a future PR wires a reader, at which point every token issued since this change must be handled under the already-frozen format.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId hardcodes the wire format with no version field: it requires encodedContext.length() == 6 and slices positionally (0-2/2-4/4-6), so the format's only identity is its length. Adding any further context dimension (which the SPI javadoc explicitly anticipates) forces a second length-based parse branch, and every token issued with the 6-char format becomes a permanently-parsed legacy variant — the 'framework' freezes a 3-dimension, 6-character budget with no in-band extension mechanism.

[ADVISORY] Decoding is asymmetric: a legacy ID without ':' degrades to UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/'na', but an encoded ID whose shortcut is not registered throws IllegalArgumentException out of getTokenContextFromTokenId. Tokens issued while a feature-gated grant was enabled become undecodable after the grant is disabled — PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory is registered only when the OID4VC_VCI feature is on (its isSupported), so 'pc' tokens throw instead of degrading the way legacy tokens do; the lazy-refresh fallback cannot rescue this because the factory itself is unregistered.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut()'s javadoc instructs 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the wire format allots exactly 2 characters, and postInit validates shortcut uniqueness (via map-size comparison) without validating shortcut width. A grant factory written to the javadoc registers successfully and encodeTokenId emits a 7-char context, after which getTokenContextFromTokenId throws 'Expected length of 6' for every token that grant issued — permanently undecodable tokens from a registration the framework accepted.

[ADVISORY] Context.grantType is derived once in the constructor (formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE)) and never re-derived, while the existing setFormParams method replaces formParams without updating it. Any flow that swaps the form params after Context construction stamps clientSessionCtx — and hence the encoded token ID — with the previous request's grant type; the class now holds two sources of truth for the request's grant that its own public setter desyncs silently.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are unreachable: Keycloak registers all providers before postInit and never hot-deploys them, so any factory findable via sessionFactory at runtime was already in postInit's getProviderFactoriesStream. Roughly 25 lines of dead defensive code that mutate the shared shortcut maps without the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit enforces, and re-scan every grant factory on each miss; deleting both branches leaves observable behavior identical for every reachable input (unknown grant/shortcut still terminates in the same IllegalStateException/IllegalArgumentException).

[ADVISORY] No test exercises getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (TRANSIENT-vs-offline precedence, lightweight detection, 'na' fallback) or the factory's postInit registry construction and duplicate-shortcut validation; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest hand-builds grantsByShortcuts and never calls postInit. A regression in session-type detection or registry building ships green; the test's negative case (testIncorrectGrantType) actually passes via a NullPointerException — sessionFactory is null because postInit was skipped — not via the intended IllegalArgumentException, so it would stay green even if the validation path broke entirely.

[ADVISORY] getShouldUseLightweightToken is widened from package-private instance method to public static solely so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider (a different package) can call it, coupling the encoder SPI's token-type determination to a mapper-base-class internal. The SPI's input (ClientSessionContext) under-determines its output (tokenType), so every TokenContextEncoderProvider implementation must reach into org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.mappers to reproduce lightweight detection or mis-classify tokens; the just-widened public static becomes de-facto API that cannot be moved or narrowed without breaking encoder implementations.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId checks the wrong character offset (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6) — the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix) AND inverts the comparison (returns false on equality instead of on inequality), so the grant-shortcut assertion never fires and verifies nothing. All four updated expectations (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass regardless of which grant shortcut the token ID carries, so a regression that mislabels or drops the grant wiring (e.g., a grant path that stops setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE and silently falls back to 'na') ships undetected; and if the equality branch ever does fire (future shortcut mix), correct tokens are rejected because the logic is inverted. With current shortcuts substring(3,5) always yields 't'+first-char-of-grant, which equals none of ac/cc/pg/pc/rt/ro/te/ci/dg, so the check is dead code.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second check, intended to validate rawTokenId (message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'), validates grantType again, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. The rawTokenId not-null invariant is unenforced: a null rawTokenId flows through construction and encodeTokenId produces a token id ending in the literal string 'null' (':' + null concatenation) instead of failing fast at the constructor.

[ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally routes every access token ID through the encoder, changing the externally visible jti format from a plain UUID to 'xxxxxx:uuid' for all tokens on all realms, with no feature flag, no realm/client-level toggle, no isSupported gate on DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, and no shipped no-op provider to revert to. A PR titled 'implement framework' also silently flips the default token-ID format for every deployment on upgrade; downstream consumers that parse or validate jti as a UUID (log pipelines, SIEM rules, external libraries) break, and during rolling upgrades clusters emit mixed formats. Operators who hit an incompatibility cannot disable the behavior without deploying custom provider code, since the only registered provider is the default and selecting a nonexistent provider id makes session.getProvider return null and initToken NPE.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the session-type classification (TRANSIENT/offline/online), the lightweight-token decision via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, and the null-grant 'na' fallback — has zero test coverage; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest constructs the provider with a null session, so this method cannot even be invoked without NPE. A regression in session-type or token-type classification (e.g., offline sessions labeled ONLINE, lightweight tokens labeled REGULAR) would silently misclassify every issued token ID with no failing test, corrupting the data the decode-side consumers of this framework are meant to rely on.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut are unreachable — the provider registry is fixed after postInit and postInit already populated both maps from the same getProviderFactoriesStream, so any factory findable via getProviderFactory was already in the maps — and if ever reached they mutate the maps without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation. Dead code misleads maintainers into believing runtime map refresh works within a running server, and the latent path would overwrite an existing shortcut entry in grantsByShortcuts on a shortcut collision (making getGrantTypeByShortcut decode that shortcut to the wrong grant) while bypassing the postInit IllegalStateException guard; both branches pass the deletion test (removing them leaves behavior identical, since a true miss already yields null and the ISE in encodeTokenId).

[BUG] The constructor's fourth guard is a copy-paste error: it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time instead of checking rawTokenId, so the rawTokenId null-check is dead code. A null rawTokenId passes validation and encodeTokenId() then emits the literal string 'null' as the unique token suffix (e.g. jti 'onrtac:null'), collapsing jti uniqueness for every such token; the guard that exists to prevent this never fires. There is also no empty-string check, so a rawId of '' producing 'onrtac:' is accepted too.

[ADVISORY] initToken now unconditionally encodes session type (online/offline/transient), token type (lightweight/regular) and the OAuth grant type into the access token jti, which is stored world-readable in the JWT payload decodable by any bearer without the signing key. Every resource server, browser-side script, or party that captures a bearer token can decode deployment and flow metadata not previously disclosed in the token — e.g. that a client authenticates via the password grant ('ro') or that the holder has an offline/transient session; this is the feature's stated intent, but it is an unconditional disclosure with no realm/client-level opt-out, so the tradeoff should be an explicit, documented decision rather than a side effect of the jti format change.

[ADVISORY] The encode-direction logic — session-type derivation (transient/offline/online), lightweight-token detection via the newly-public getShouldUseLightweightToken, and the null-grant fallback to 'na' — plus postInit's shortcut-map building and duplicate-shortcut validation have no test coverage in this diff; the new test class only exercises decode/encode round-trips against hand-seeded maps with a null session. A regression in context derivation (e.g. offline sessions encoded as 'on', or the lightweight check flipping) would silently mislabel the jti of every subsequently issued token — exactly the data future consumers of getTokenContextFromTokenId will trust — and a duplicate-shortcut regression would only surface as a server startup failure instead of being caught in CI.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher never verifies the grant shortcut it claims to check: it reads items[0].substring(3, 5) (the second char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant shortcut, instead of the grant's actual position at indices 4-5, i.e. substring(4, 6)), and the comparison is inverted (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the ID when the grant matches), so the grant-check branch is unreachable for every real shortcut combination (char index 3 is always 't' for token types 'rt'/'lt', which can never equal a shortcut starting with 'a'/'c'/'r'/'d'/'p'). The four event helpers this diff rewires to the new format (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) now assert only 'exactly one colon + UUID suffix' — they pass regardless of which grant shortcut TokenManager.initToken/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encoded, so a regression that writes the wrong grant (or the wrong session/token-type chars) into every access-token ID ships with a green suite; the grant-level assertion these parameterized matchers were added to provide is void, and no other test in the diff verifies any grant shortcut end-to-end.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the half of the encoder that derives SessionType (TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE vs ONLINE), TokenType (LIGHTWEIGHT vs REGULAR via getShouldUseLightweightToken), and the UNKNOWN-grant fallback — has zero test coverage: the only test file in the diff referencing these symbols, services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, never constructs a ClientSessionContext and never calls this method (it exercises only getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId), and the AssertEvents matchers ignore the encoded prefix entirely. A regression that classifies offline-user-session tokens as ONLINE, flips the lightweight/regular decision, or drops the null-grant fallback passes the entire suite; downstream consumers relying on the encoded context (the feature's stated purpose: recovering token context without proprietary claims) read wrong session/token-type data with no failing test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The test fixture bypasses DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit entirely (only init(null) is called) and hand-assigns the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps with 2 of the 9 real grants, so the factory's production wiring — populating the maps from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException validation, and both lazy-refresh cache-miss paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (which require the sessionFactory field that postInit sets) — is never executed by any test in the diff. A new grant provider deployed with a colliding shortcut (the exact scenario the postInit validation comment names) or the runtime map-refresh path for a newly deployed grant fails at server startup or mis-encodes token IDs with no failing test; the hand-poked fixture is a mirror of production wiring that diverges from it (production inserts all grant factories plus the UNKNOWN entry), so the tests validate a fixture, not the initialization code.

[ADVISORY] Three of the four rejection branches in getTokenContextFromTokenId are untested: the encodedContext.length() != 6 guard (line 74), the unknown session-type shortcut (line 83), and the unknown token-type shortcut (line 87) are never triggered by any test in the diff — the only negative test, testIncorrectGrantType in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, covers solely the unknown-grant branch. A regression that accepts a prefix of a length other than 6 silently mis-slices the fixed 2-2-2 layout and decodes a valid-looking but wrong context (e.g., grant type read from the wrong offset) with no failing test, and an unknown session/token-type shortcut regression in the factory shortcut tables goes undetected.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException broadly and ignores it (the variable is even named `iae`), so any runtime exception — an NPE or ClassCastException from a refactor bug in the parsing path — satisfies the test, and the actual contract (IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant shortcut, thrown at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 91-93) is not pinned, in contrast to testOldToken in the same file which correctly catches the specific IllegalStateException. A future regression that makes getTokenContextFromTokenId throw a different unchecked exception for the wrong reason still passes this test, masking the breakage until token validation fails at runtime.

[BUG] The constructor's null-guard for rawTokenId is a copy-paste error: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) is invoked twice, so the second call (message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') re-validates grantType and rawTokenId is never checked. A null rawTokenId passes the constructor's documented invariant and flows into encodeTokenId, which string-concatenates it into a token ID ending in the literal ':null' (and getTokenContextFromTokenId would return a context with rawTokenId=null), instead of failing fast as the guard promises — the validation this new framework API relies on silently does not exist for one of its four fields.

[ADVISORY] postInit invokes the newly added, default-less OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() on every registered grant factory, breaking binary compatibility with any grant provider compiled against the previous version of the interface. On a node running this build, a pre-existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory jar (old bytecode lacking getShortcut) throws AbstractMethodError at the gtf.getShortcut() call during startup, so the node fails to boot during a rolling upgrade — a failure that previously would have surfaced as a per-request unsupported-grant error, not a hard startup failure.

[ADVISORY] The access-token jti format is cut over unconditionally from a plain UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' with no compatibility flag or rollout gate, changing the format of the persisted event detail Details.TOKEN_ID for every token issued after the upgrade. Event-store rows written post-upgrade carry 'onrtac:<uuid>'-style token_id values alongside pre-upgrade UUID rows with no transition period; consumers that assume the UUID format break at cutover — the diff itself had to replace isUUID() with isAccessTokenId() in four AssertEvents matchers, proving the in-tree UUID assumption, and external audit/SIEM tooling parsing KEYCLOAK_EVENT details gets no fallback or rollback lever (the default encoder always encodes).

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and then returns false when that substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, so the grant check is simultaneously offset-wrong and logically inverted; because index 3 is always 't' (tokenType shortcuts 'rt'/'lt') and none of the expected shortcuts ('ac', 'dg', 'rt', 'ci') starts with 't', the equals comparison can never be true and the matcher degenerates to only checking 'exactly one colon + UUID tail'. All four updated event matchers (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) accept a token ID carrying any grant shortcut (or 'na'), so a regression that encodes the wrong grant into access-token jtis passes the entire integration suite silently while the tests appear to assert grant context; additionally, a context prefix shorter than 5 chars makes substring(3,5) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match.

[BUG] The second Objects.requireNonNull in the constructor checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId, so the rawTokenId null guard is dead code and the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' message can never be produced for rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and encodeTokenId concatenates it into a token ID ending in ':null', corrupting the jti instead of failing fast at construction as the guard intends.

[ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts with no format validation — there is no check that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() returns exactly 2 characters — even though getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires a 6-char context (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException for any other length. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployed as a provider with a 1- or 3-char shortcut passes startup validation, and every access token that grant mints gets a structurally invalid jti that the decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, breaking the decode path for those tokens once getTokenContextFromTokenId is wired into request handling.

[ADVISORY] The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (and symmetrically getGrantTypeByShortcut) writes new entries into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit enforces, so a later-registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the existing shortcut→grant mapping. Tokens of the shadowed grant continue to be encoded under the colliding shortcut but decode as the newly registered grant — silent misattribution of token context with no error or log, exactly the failure mode the postInit IllegalStateException exists to prevent; the check-then-act on the ConcurrentHashMaps is also unsynchronized across threads, though concurrent identical puts are benign.

[ADVISORY] The unit test hand-populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and never calls postInit, leaving the duplicate-shortcut startup validation, both lazy-refresh paths, and getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (session-type derivation, lightweight detection, and the 'na' fallback) with no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in the collision check (e.g., weakening the size comparison) or in the lazy registry refresh ships silently; combined with the broken isAccessTokenId matcher, no test in this diff actually verifies that the grant encoded into a token ID matches the grant that issued it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts only from loaded OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances, and feature-gated grants (PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory gated on OID4VC_VCI, plus the EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory-implementing CibaGrantTypeFactory and DeviceGrantTypeFactory) are not loaded when their feature/config is off — while the lazy-refresh fallback in getGrantTypeByShortcut re-scans the same already-filtered getProviderFactoriesStream and can therefore never recover them. On a node where one of these grants is disabled, decoding a token ID carrying the 'pc'/'ci'/'dg' shortcut (issued by a node where the feature is enabled, e.g. a mixed-feature cluster once any decode consumer exists) throws IllegalArgumentException 'Unknown value ... for grant type', defeating the refresh mechanism whose stated purpose is handling grants not present in the startup maps.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts only from sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class), and getGrantTypeByShortcut()’s “refresh” path re-scans that same stream filtered by shortcut. If a grant factory is not present in that stream on a given node (e.g., due to isSupported()/environment gating on that node), then a token ID containing that grant’s shortcut will cause getGrantTypeByShortcut() to return null and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() will throw IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant shortcut. However, the claim that such gated factories are definitively excluded from getProviderFactoriesStream when disabled is not directly verifiable from the diff (it depends on Keycloak’s provider-loading semantics), so this is best treated as a real edge-case/robustness concern rather than a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the new sessionType/tokenType/grantType derivation logic — has no test in this diff that asserts its output: the unit test constructs the provider with a null session and covers only decode/encode round-trips, and the integration assertions on the encoded prefix are vacuous (see the AssertEvents matcher defect). A regression in the derivation (e.g. always classifying sessions as ONLINE/REGULAR, dropping the TRANSIENT check, or misreading the offline flag) passes the entire suite, and the mislabelled 6-char prefix would then be baked into every subsequently issued access token's jti before anyone notices.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial derivation logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` (sessionType from `UserSessionModel` persistence/offline, tokenType from `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, grantType from `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)`). The only new unit test (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`) instantiates the provider with `session = null` and exercises only `getTokenContextFromTokenId` + `encodeTokenId` round-trips, so it never asserts the derivation output. Additionally, the updated integration matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` is defective: it returns `false` when the extracted shortcut *equals* the expected one, and it slices `substring(3,5)` which does not correspond to the 2-char grant shortcut in the 6-char prefix (should be positions 4–6). This makes the integration assertions effectively not validating the intended prefix/grant classification, so regressions in derivation could slip through tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) (grant occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix) and inverts the comparison (returns false when the extracted value EQUALS the expected shortcut), so the grant assertion is vacuous. The grant-type verification this diff adds to expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken verifies nothing: for any well-formed encoded ID, substring(3,5) is always '<tokenType-2nd-char><grant-1st-char>' (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac'), which never equals 'ac'/'dg'/'rt'/'ci', so the matcher passes regardless of which grant was encoded — a regression encoding the wrong grant shortcut into every access token ID passes the whole testsuite. Additionally, if only the offset is later corrected, the inverted condition will reject every correctly encoded token, and a prefix shorter than 5 chars throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher extracts the grant shortcut using items[0].substring(3, 5), but the encoding logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId clearly defines the 6-char prefix as sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grantType(4-6). Therefore the grant shortcut should be substring(4, 6). Additionally, the matcher inverts the comparison: it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut, and otherwise proceeds to only validate the UUID portion, making the grant check effectively non-functional. The lack of a length guard also means short prefixes can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when a grant shortcut cannot be resolved, because the lazy refresh in getGrantTypeByShortcut only scans currently-registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances — so token IDs minted while a feature-gated grant was enabled ('pc' gated on OID4VC_VCI per PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory.isSupported, plus 'dg'/'ci' which are EnvironmentDependentProviderFactory) become unresolvable once that feature is disabled or the provider is removed. adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, an unresolvable grant shortcut results in an IllegalArgumentException (gt == null -> throw). Grant shortcut resolution in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory is based on currently registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances (postInit populates from getProviderFactoriesStream; getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily refreshes by scanning current factories). Therefore, if a token ID was minted with a shortcut for a grant whose factory is later not registered/available (e.g., feature/environment-dependent grants), decoding that historical token ID will throw rather than degrade to UNKNOWN (unlike the colon-less legacy format which falls back to UNKNOWN). This is a concrete robustness/backward-compatibility concern grounded in the diff, though the diff doesn’t show a concrete call path where this will break runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType (lines 113-114) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 131-132) put entries into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut validation postInit performs, so a newly registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the existing grant's mapping. In exactly the scenario this code targets ('Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed'), a colliding shortcut replaces the previous grant's entry with no error, and decoding tokens of the previously-registered grant then returns the wrong grant type — the startup IllegalStateException guard is bypassed precisely when a collision actually occurs.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the lazy refresh branches do `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` (getShortcutByGrantType) and similarly `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(newGrantType, shortcut)` (getGrantTypeByShortcut) without any collision/uniqueness check. This bypasses the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation (which only checks map sizes after initial population) and allows an existing shortcut key to be overwritten silently if a newly discovered grant uses a colliding shortcut, leading to incorrect decoding/encoding mappings.

There is no mechanism in this change that enforces every access-token minting path sets this attribute, and the encoder will still encode a token ID with the 'na' grant shortcut rather than erroring or logging, so the context can silently degrade. This is a real maintainability/coverage concern created by the change, but not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The access token jti format changes globally from a UUID to '<st><tt><gt>:<uuid>' with no feature flag, realm option, or provider configuration to disable the new format. During rolling upgrades a cluster emits two ID formats, and external consumers of jti or the TOKEN_ID event detail that assume UUIDs (an assumption Keycloak's own test suite encoded until this diff) have no opt-out short of a version downgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change access token `jti` globally: `TokenManager.initToken()` now always builds an `AccessTokenContext` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, producing `<st><tt><gt>:<rawId>` instead of a plain UUID (previous `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`). There is no conditional/flag/realm-option in the shown code path to retain the old UUID format, and the tests were adjusted to stop asserting UUIDs for `Details.TOKEN_ID`, indicating a compatibility break. However, this is primarily a backwards-compat/upgrade/architecture concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff itself (the change appears intentional and internally compensated by updated tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit invokes the newly added, default-less OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() on every registered grant factory, breaking binary compatibility with any grant provider compiled against the previous version of the interface. On a node running this build, a pre-existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory jar (old bytecode lacking getShortcut) throws AbstractMethodError at the gtf.getShortcut() call during startup, so the node fails to boot during a rolling upgrade — a failure that previously would have surfaced as a per-request unsupported-grant error, not a hard startup failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. That is binary-incompatible for any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the previous interface (their bytecode won’t have `getShortcut`). The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally invokes `gtf.getShortcut()`, which will trigger `AbstractMethodError` for such older implementations during startup (`postInit`), potentially preventing the node from booting. This is directly supported by the interface change and the new call site in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The access-token jti format is cut over unconditionally from a plain UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' with no compatibility flag or rollout gate, changing the format of the persisted event detail Details.TOKEN_ID for every token issued after the upgrade. Event-store rows written post-upgrade carry 'onrtac:<uuid>'-style token_id values alongside pre-upgrade UUID rows with no transition period; consumers that assume the UUID format break at cutover — the diff itself had to replace isUUID() with isAccessTokenId() in four AssertEvents matchers, proving the in-tree UUID assumption, and external audit/SIEM tooling parsing KEYCLOAK_EVENT details gets no fallback or rollback lever (the default encoder always encodes).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AccessToken.id (jti) generation from a raw UUID to an encoded form `(<6-char-context>):(<rawId>)` unconditionally in `TokenManager.initToken()` by always calling `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` (no feature flag/gate shown). The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` always prepends the context and `:` and will throw if types are unknown, so the format change is real and immediate. Tests in `AssertEvents` were updated from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(...)`, corroborating that `Details.TOKEN_ID` now carries the new format. However, the diff does not show an internal Keycloak regression beyond this intentional format change; the concern is rollout/compatibility for external consumers rather than a verifiable functional defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and then returns false when that substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, so the grant check is simultaneously offset-wrong and logically inverted; because index 3 is always 't' (tokenType shortcuts 'rt'/'lt') and none of the expected shortcuts ('ac', 'dg', 'rt', 'ci') starts with 't', the equals comparison can never be true and the matcher degenerates to only checking 'exactly one colon + UUID tail'. All four updated event matchers (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) accept a token ID carrying any grant shortcut (or 'na'), so a regression that encodes the wrong grant into access-token jtis passes the entire integration suite silently while the tests appear to assert grant context; additionally, a context prefix shorter than 5 chars makes substring(3,5) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the match.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context format (per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider) is 6 chars: [0..2)=sessionType, [2..4)=tokenType, [4..6)=grantType. The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5) (off by one) and then returns false when that substring *equals* expectedGrantShortcut, which inverts the intended check (it should fail when it does NOT equal). As written, it will accept mismatched grant shortcuts (and may even reject correct ones depending on characters), so the updated event assertions no longer reliably validate the grant shortcut in the token ID. Also, substring(3,5) can throw if the prefix is shorter than 5 chars, causing an exception rather than a clean mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second Objects.requireNonNull in the constructor checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId, so the rawTokenId null guard is dead code and the 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' message can never be produced for rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and encodeTokenId concatenates it into a token ID ending in ':null', corrupting the jti instead of failing fast at construction as the guard intends.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null guard intended for `rawTokenId` is incorrect: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (diff hunk in `AccessTokenContext.java`). As a result, `rawTokenId` can be null and no exception will be thrown at construction. Later, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield a token id ending with `":null"` rather than failing fast, matching the finding’s described corruption risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit registers grant shortcuts with no format validation — there is no check that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() returns exactly 2 characters — even though getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires a 6-char context (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException for any other length. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployed as a provider with a 1- or 3-char shortcut passes startup validation, and every access token that grant mints gets a structurally invalid jti that the decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, breaking the decode path for those tokens once getTokenContextFromTokenId is wired into request handling.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(), the decoder hard-requires the pre-':' context to be exactly 6 chars (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. However DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() records OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() values with only a uniqueness check (map size comparison) and no validation that the shortcut is exactly 2 characters. encodeTokenId() then concatenates sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShort(with arbitrary length), so a custom grant with 1 or 3 chars would mint JTIs that cannot be decoded by getTokenContextFromTokenId(), creating an internal encode/decode inconsistency. This is compounded by the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc explicitly suggesting “3-letters shortcut”, which would produce invalid IDs under the current decoder assumptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (and symmetrically getGrantTypeByShortcut) writes new entries into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit enforces, so a later-registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the existing shortcut→grant mapping. Tokens of the shadowed grant continue to be encoded under the colliding shortcut but decode as the newly registered grant — silent misattribution of token context with no error or log, exactly the failure mode the postInit IllegalStateException exists to prevent; the check-then-act on the ConcurrentHashMaps is also unsynchronized across threads, though concurrent identical puts are benign.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() builds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and enforces uniqueness via a size-equality check. However, the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() can later do grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) / grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut) without any duplicate-shortcut (or duplicate-id) validation. If a newly available OAuth2GrantTypeFactory has a shortcut that collides with an existing one, the ConcurrentHashMap put will silently overwrite the prior shortcut→grant mapping, causing subsequent decoding (getGrantTypeByShortcut) to resolve that shortcut to the newer grant type (misattribution) with no error/log—exactly what postInit’s validation is intended to prevent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The unit test hand-populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and never calls postInit, leaving the duplicate-shortcut startup validation, both lazy-refresh paths, and getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (session-type derivation, lightweight detection, and the 'na' fallback) with no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in the collision check (e.g., weakening the size comparison) or in the lazy registry refresh ships silently; combined with the broken isAccessTokenId matcher, no test in this diff actually verifies that the grant encoded into a token ID matches the grant that issued it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s key claim that the new `isAccessTokenId` matcher is broken is verifiable in the diff. In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, it extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)` even though the encoded context is 6 chars with grant shortcut in positions 4–5 (0-based), i.e. should be `substring(4, 6)`. Additionally it returns `false` when the extracted substring equals the expected shortcut (`if (...) return false;`), which is inverted logic. As a result, the matcher effectively only checks that the raw part after `:` is a UUID and does not validate the grant type, so the updated event assertions don’t actually verify grant-specific token IDs as intended.
